subject: Cloud region evacuation notice and traffic re-home steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@finco.com>, ops-team@acme.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Cloud region evacuation notice and traffic re-home steps

Hi Alice / FinCo ops team —

Quick update from Redwood infra: we are seeing a persistent peering degradation affecting EU-west1 (eu-west1) and APAC-northeast1 (ap-northeast1) across one of our backbone providers. Impact: increased tail latency and intermittent connection resets for clients routing to those zones.

For any production traffic we recommend an immediate, temporary re-home of traffic away from eu-west1/ap-northeast1 to our alternate endpoints while we stabilize the peering. Expected mitigation window is 6–12 hours; we will provide updates on the status page and through this thread.

Recommended steps (conservative, minimal-change path):
1) Preferred-region header: if you can set headers, add X-Redwood-Region: us-west1 (or eu-central1) on outgoing requests for the next 6 hours. This forces routing preference without client config changes.
2) SDK env var: set REDWOOD_PREFERRED_REGIONS="us-west1,eu-central1" in your app environment so SDKs prefer healthy regions.
3) Retries and timeouts: increase client-side per-request timeout by +500ms and set 2 retries for transient errors. Avoid long-poll connections during the re-home window.
4) Connection pools: gracefully drain persistent connections to eu-west1 (close after current request).
5) Verification: run the attached traffic-verification-script.sh from a staging host to confirm requests land in the target region and TLS negotiation is fine.

We attach a short checklist and the IP ranges for the alternate endpoints (alt-endpoints-ip-ranges.json). Vanessa has signed off on cert continuity for the alternate endpoints (no cert re-issue required).

If you cannot make these changes immediately, we can enable a server-side fallback on your behalf for the next 6 hours — that will prefer us-west1 for your tenant at the routing layer. Please confirm which option you prefer (self-run or Redwood-assisted) and a target cutover window.

I will be on this thread and on call with Vanessa for the next several hours.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-reroute-checklist.pdf, alt-endpoints-ip-ranges.json, traffic-verification-script.sh

From: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@finco.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@acme.com
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 10:15:23 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud region evacuation notice and traffic re-home steps

Neha — thanks for the quick heads-up. A couple of quick questions: 

- Will TLS certificates and SAN entries remain valid if we route to us-west1/eu-central1? We cannot roll certs mid-day.
- Can you confirm the IP ranges that might be used by the alternate endpoints? We need to update our egress ACLs.
- If you enable Redwood-assisted fallback, will that be rolling (some traffic) or all traffic immediately? We prefer a short, <15 minute maintenance window for a full cutover if possible.

Quoted for context:
> Quick update from Redwood infra: we are seeing a persistent peering degradation affecting EU-west1 (eu-west1) and APAC-northeast1 (ap-northeast1) across one of our backbone providers. Impact: increased tail latency and intermittent connection resets for clients routing to those zones.

We can run the checklist but want to be sure about certs and ACLs first.

Best,
Alice
Head of Platform Engineering
FinCo

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@finco.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 13:05:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud region evacuation notice and traffic re-home steps

Hi Alice — short answers:

- TLS / certs: confirmed. The certificates presented at our alternate endpoints include the same SANs for your tenant bindings; no cert reissue required. We validated this at 12:35 UTC.
- IP ranges: see attached alt-endpoints-ip-ranges.json (these are the CIDR blocks our edge layer will advertise for the alternate endpoints). If you need a signed proof-of-origin, we can provide it via the compliance team.
- Fallback mode: Redwood-assisted fallback can be configured in two ways:
   a) gradual (recommended): route 10% -> 50% -> 100% over a 30 minute window with health checks and automatic rollback on error.
   b) immediate cutover: route 100% immediately (we can schedule a maintenance window).

If you prefer an immediate maintenance window, tell us the preferred start time and we'll coordinate a brief 15-minute window and monitor the runbook. Otherwise we recommend gradual ramp to reduce risk.

Verification checklist (high level):
- Run traffic-verification-script.sh from a host mimicking production egress.
- Confirm TLS handshake and the returned region header X-Redwood-Region in responses.
- Confirm 0% TLS cert errors and <1% 5xx during ramp.

I'll stay on standby to execute the assisted fallback if you give the go-ahead.

—Vanessa
Principal Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: alt-endpoints-ip-ranges.json, traffic-verification-script.sh

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Zhao <alice.zhao@finco.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jul 2028 15:40:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud region evacuation notice and traffic re-home steps

Alice — thanks for the quick reply and great questions.

We will proceed per your preference: you indicated a short <15 minute maintenance window is preferable. Please propose a start time in the next 2 hours (we recommend 16:00 PT / 23:00 UTC) and we will schedule the assisted immediate cutover with a 15-minute hold and active monitoring.

Action items for FinCo (self-serve) if you want to run first:
- Run traffic-verification-script.sh and paste the output into this thread (the script verifies region header and TLS).
- Update egress ACLs with the attached alt-endpoints-ip-ranges.json prior to the selected window.

If you want Redwood to perform the cutover, reply with the chosen start time and we will:
1) Enable routing change at the edge for your tenant.
2) Monitor metrics (latency, 5xx, TLS errors) and rollback on automated thresholds.
3) Share an after-action note with timestamps and verification logs.

We will also publish an interim post-incident note on the status page and a full postmortem after the issue is resolved.

Thanks — I will hold the slot for 16:00 PT if you don't object.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-reroute-checklist.pdf (runbook excerpt), traffic-verification-script.sh (small verification helper)
